data.name: Protection
data.description: A grain merchant has been paying someone every eighth day for two years. He reported it last week because the price went up. He has never been given a name. Stand three nights at his yard and make sure nobody collects.
data.successDescription: Whoever runs it never visits the yard and never meets his own men. A loose stone in a wall is the only place he has to be.

objectives.description:
A guard posting on the board. Three nights at a grain yard on the north row, starting tonight.

The slip reads: C rank. Make sure nobody collects.

A ledger column. Every eighth day, for two years, the same amount, written down as cartage costs.

The merchant reported it last week. The note says he did it because the price went up, not because he wanted to.

Nobody knows who takes the money. He has never been given a name, and he has never asked for one.

The yard is grain sacks, a weighbridge, a street front, and a back gate onto a lane.

The merchant meets you at the weighbridge and does not shake your hand.

"Back gate, after close. It is never the same man twice."

"Two years I have paid it, and I want you to understand why. It was less than a burnt yard, and there was nobody to report. You cannot hand a hall a man with no name and expect them to write anything down."

"Then the price went up, and I could put a number on it, and a number is a thing a hall will read."

"I want three quiet nights, and then I want you gone. I would like to be honest with you about that."

The yard goes quiet after the last cart, and the lane behind the gate goes quiet after that.

You can stand where the lane can see you, or you can be somewhere it cannot.
You take the gate and stand where the whole lane can see you.

Nothing comes up the lane. A man walks past the mouth of it once, does not slow down, and does not come back.

One evening the merchant closes early and does not say why.
You take the gate again and stand in it for six hours.

Nobody comes up the lane at all.

And now you understand it. Nothing is going to come up that lane while you are standing in it. Whoever keeps walking past its mouth understands it too.
You put yourself behind the sack stack with the gate in view, and you let the lane look exactly the way it looked last month.

Two come up the lane a little after midnight.

One goes to the gate. The other stops twenty feet short and stands facing back the way they came. He does not look at the gate once.

One collector. One lookout.

The one at the gate has a hand on the latch when you come off the stack. The lookout is already turning.

Neither of them runs. They have done this enough times to know that running is what gets you chased.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
Two of them at a back gate in the dark, and the yard is a bad place to be outnumbered.

The gate stands open when you get up, and the lane is empty. Inside the house a lamp goes on, and then goes off again. The merchant has decided not to come out.

In the morning he pays the hall for more nights. He does not look at you while he does it.

The collector sits against the gate post and does not pretend to be anything else. He lets you go through his coat. There is nothing in it but a folded cloth for carrying coin and a stub of wax.

He answers everything, flat. Nobody sent him. He takes the pickup and keeps a fixed cut of it. He has never met the man he leaves it for.

He works out what the answer is worth to him, and gives it anyway.

A drop. A loose stone in a wall, and he has never once seen who empties it. The man does not come to the yard, and he does not meet the men who do.

That is the whole design. A collector who has met him could describe him, and a man who can be described can be sold. A stone cannot be questioned and does not want a cut.

And if you take him in tonight, someone new is standing on this gate in eight days.

He walks in without arguing and gives a statement that is short and true.

Extortion, a name on a docket, and a merchant who gets a season of quiet out of it.

The handler logs the charge and pays out the posting.

"He cannot name anyone above him, because there is no one above him he has ever seen."

"It is a real charge, and it stops exactly here. That is where these things usually stop."

nextObjectiveId.text: A charge, and it stops there.

objectives.description:
He takes you to it, because the other choice is a cell, and he has already decided which he prefers.

Four streets away, a dead wall behind a barrel maker's yard, and a stone at knee height that comes out clean. The space behind it is dry and worn smooth.

You report it to the hall.

"No arrest. The merchant keeps paying for a few more weeks while somebody watches a wall."

"You let a collection happen. You also brought back the one thing in this that does not move."

Three nights, no collection, a full ledger.

The handler signs the posting off and pays out without comment.

On the last morning the merchant walks you to the gate and stops there.

"They will be back when you are not. I am not blaming you. I want you to know that I know it."

nextObjectiveId.text: Three quiet nights, and then gone.

objectives.description: Three nights stood.
The yard after close, and the lane behind the gate.

data.name: The Loud Way
data.description: Eleven crates signed into a bonded warehouse in four months and never signed out. Nobody reports a theft, and nobody pays four months of bond fees on goods they never touch. Get inside, learn what the building is for, get out.
data.successDescription: The warehouse was never storing anything. It is a place where two people who refuse to meet can hand something over without ever being in the room at the same time.

objectives.description:
B rank on the board. Infiltration, a bonded warehouse on the canal.

You take it to the desk, and the handler sends you upstairs instead. Jobs that go upstairs are not ordinary jobs.

A small room, two ledgers open side by side, and an officer who does not introduce herself.

"Eleven crates in four months. Signed into the bonded yard, never signed out. Nobody has reported a theft. And nobody pays four months of bond fees on goods they never touch."

"Get in, learn what the building is for, get out. B rank, because the people on that yard at night are not amateurs."

nextObjectiveId.text: I will find my own way in.

objectives.description:
Three ways in, and she recommends none of them.

The roofline carries a lookout on the canal side who does not leave when the shift does. The street door is lit, with two men on it on the nights crates move. The canal drain comes up inside the building, and costs an hour on your hands and knees.

"One more thing. The yard hired extra men for tonight. Whatever this building is for, tonight it is for something."
Four ways at it. The night is not getting longer.
The customs office keeps the bond book, and will show it to anyone with a tasking.

Every one of the eleven is signed, sealed, and lawful. The paperwork is perfect.

You have spent an hour learning that the paper will tell you nothing. Whatever is wrong in that building, it is not written down.
The roofline runs unbroken from the barrel maker's to the warehouse gable. You take it slowly, because the lookout is sitting on the far end of it.

They come off the chimney fast and light, and they do not shout. Shouting would tell the whole canal that the roof was watched.

This one intends to leave quietly, and would rather go over you than past you.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They break over the gable and are three streets gone before you are upright.

Below, the street door stays lit and nobody comes out of it. Whatever they saw, they have not told anyone yet.

Two in identical blank half masks, standing in the light, watching you cross the whole width of the street without once looking at each other.

Neither moves until you are inside arm's reach. Then both move at once.

They are not fast, and they are not trying to be. The doorway is eight feet wide, and they intend to still be standing in it when this finishes.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
Eight feet of doorway, and two people who will not step out of it.

They do not follow you when you go. That is the part that stays with you.

You are on the loading floor inside a minute, which is faster than either of the other ways in.

Every window on the canal now knows the warehouse had something worth guarding. The floor is stacked four high with bonded crates, and every seal on them is unbroken.

nextObjectiveId.text: Work the stacks by seal date.

objectives.description: The canal drain runs under the loading floor and comes up inside the building. An hour on your hands and knees, in water that has been standing since spring.

You come up through the hatch with your boots full of canal, and nobody has heard a thing.

Beside the nearest stack there is a ring in the dust where a man knelt, and the knee print is still damp from the canal fog.

Someone was in here while you were in the water.

The floor is stacked four high with bonded crates, and every seal on them is unbroken.

The building is a quarter full. The eleven are not hidden. They are standing in the open with all the rest.

nextObjectiveId.text: Work the stacks by seal date.

objectives.description: The eleven are not together and not in sequence. Finding what they have in common takes most of an hour.

Every one of them has been opened and resealed. The seals are genuine.

The crates are empty.

A man walks in with a thing and puts it in a crate. He leaves. Days later, a different man opens the crate and takes the thing out. The two are never in the building at the same time, and neither one can name a person he has never met.

Beside the eleventh crate there is a manifest sheet, lying face down, belonging to no crate at all.

Eleven collection times, written in one steady, unhurried hand.

The last time on the sheet is tonight.

nextObjectiveId.text: Put the sheet back and get up in the rafters.

objectives.description: You fold the sheet into your coat and go for the canal door.

Nine steps from it, the street door opens behind you, and does not close.

Nobody says anything. That is worse than if they had.
You go up the stacks into the roof space, settle where the floor cannot see you, and give it the rest of the night.

The canal door opens without a sound.

One person, alone, walking straight to the eleventh crate without looking at anything else in the building. They crouch to read the manifest, and they do not pick it up.

They have not made a noise since the door, and they are not going to.

Three of them, fanning out across the floor without a word. They were not sent to collect a crate. They were sent to make sure the collection was not interrupted.

They can see the corner of the sheet in your coat from where they are standing.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
Three across an open floor is too many, and they know it.

One of them takes the sheet off you, walks it back to the eleventh crate, and lays it down face down, exactly where it was. Then all three step back into the dark of the stacks and wait.

They were paid for the whole night. So were you.
They know you are in the roof before your feet leave it.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They put you on the floor without a sound, finish reading, and go out the way they came in, empty handed.

They were not the collection. They came ahead of it, to check that the way was clear.

nextObjectiveId.text: Stay put. Wait for the collection.

objectives.description:
Eleven entries over four months, and beside each one a figure that is not a price.

Two days. Six days. Nine days.

It is a delay. The crate holds the thing until enough time has passed. Nobody was paying for storage. They were paying for the distance between two hands.

That is what the bond fee is buying. Four months of lawful, boring, receipted storage, so that the wait between one man and the next looks like paperwork instead of a meeting.

Because a meeting is two faces in one room, and a room can be described afterwards by anybody who was standing in it. These people do not know each other, and this building is how they keep it that way.

nextObjectiveId.text: Burn the eleven and close the route tonight.
Leave the floor exactly as I found it.

objectives.description:
Eleven crates go up on the loading floor, and the canal watch puts the fire out before it reaches the stacks. By morning the warehouse is a customs incident.

"Route closed, warehouse under review, and everyone who used it knows we found it."

She signs it off.

"It is a result, and I will take it. In six days they will be using a different bonded warehouse, and we will be looking at nothing."

nextObjectiveId.text: Route closed, and everyone knows it.

objectives.description:
You put the floor back down to the ring in the dust, and go out through the drain with the manifest copied and the original lying face down.

She reads the copy and stops at the last line.

"Six days."

She leaves a finger on it.

"They do not know we were in the building. In six days, somebody walks in and collects while we are standing in the roof."

"You could have had a case tonight. You brought me a date. Do not do that again without asking. And thank you."

nextObjectiveId.text: Six days, and nobody knows we were there.

objectives.description: Warehouse read.
The floor, the eleventh crate, and the manifest.
Four ways at it, and the night is not getting longer.

data.name: WEDGE_PROBE_D_coordswap
data.description: The keeper of the pass waystation is going home to open it again. The posting says: guard her from bandits, two days up the pass road. The pay is low, even for C rank.
data.successDescription: The posting said bandits. It was never bandits.

objectives.description:
A posting on the board: an escort, two days up the pass road. Guard the client from bandits.

The slip reads: C rank. One traveler. The pay is low, even for C rank.

The client is the keeper of the waystation at the top of the pass. She ran it for thirty years, and now she is going back up to open it again.

The handler has added a note by hand: she asked twice whether an escort is released if a job turns out worse than its posting. She asked it like someone who already knew the answer.

The keeper waits at the village gate with a pack of tools, no valuables, and a straight back. She sets off without being told, and she does not look behind her once.

The low road runs past the toll shed toward the foot of the pass.

nextObjectiveId.text: Ask at the toll shed first.

objectives.description:
You stop at the toll shed and let the toll man talk. He talks about bandit trouble easily, at length, and a little too readily.

In the whole conversation, he never once asks who you are guarding.

Where the road narrows, you read the ground. A fire pit, two days cold. Cut stems at boot height on both sides of the track. A flat stone worn smooth where a man sat for hours, facing downhill, toward the village.

Bandits watch a road for whoever comes along it. These men were waiting for someone.

They come out of the cut brush on both sides at once. Rags over their mouths, no plates on their foreheads.

They fight like men paid by the day. The moment it turns, the paid day is over.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
Two sides at once is one side too many, and they know this ground.

They pull back down the slope and re-form where the road narrows. They are paid to hold this stretch, so they will be standing in it again.

Bandits rob whoever the road brings them. These men were placed on the one road one woman has to take, days before she took it.

And a shut waystation still has a road under it. Somebody has spent a year standing on that road taking what the station used to take, and writing none of it down. An open door at the top of the pass ends that on the first morning.

The posting said bandits. The posting was wrong. And the rule on every slip is plain: a false posting frees the escort. You may turn back now, paid for the road you walked, with no fault written against you.

The keeper has not stopped walking.

"I wrote bandits. Bandits is what I could afford."

nextObjectiveId.text: Turn back. The posting was false.

objectives.description:
Above the ambush ground the way splits.

The pass road climbs wide and open, in view of the ridge the whole way. The old stair cut goes straight up through the rocks: steep, narrow, and out of sight.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the pass road, and watch the ridge.

objectives.description:
You put the keeper behind a boulder and watch the ridge line.

A shape against the sky holds still for a long time. Then it gives up waiting, and moves to where the pass narrows.

Two of them at the neck of the pass. The younger one stands the way the first two stood.

The other one holds his ground like a man who was trained once, and remembers most of it.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
The stair cut is four hundred steps of broken stone with grass growing through them.

You climb with the keeper's hand on your shoulder, and you come out above the pass, behind everything that is watching it.

One man sits at the top of the stair with his back against the waystation wall, out of the wind.

He was paid to make sure nobody reached this door. Nobody told him about the stair. Now he has to earn the money, and he does not like it.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
The high ground wins, and the pass throws you back down to the fork.

The keeper waits there with her pack still on. She does not say anything. She simply waits to go up again.

The waystation door has been shut for a year, and it opens on the first pull.

The keeper walks the rooms once, opens the shutters, and lays a fire in the cold hearth like she never left.

When you reach the first bend of the road down, there is already smoke standing up from the chimney behind you.

You bring the keeper back down and set the slip on the desk with the release written under it.

The handler reads it, signs it off without comment, and pays out the road you walked.

She goes back up the pass alone the next morning. You are not told how it ends.

nextObjectiveId.text: The posting was false. Release taken.

objectives.description:
The handler reads the report twice. The false posting. The prepared ground. A year of tolls collected at an empty station.

"A false posting frees the escort. You knew that, and you finished the road anyway."

"That is worth knowing about a person. And someone will be walking up to ask about those tolls."
Road walked, station open.
The road narrows, and the ground still reads the same.
The fork below the pass.
